name: Chai Theory
oneLiner: A modern chai cafe chain doing PKR 2.8M a month across three Karachi locations.
problem: Karachi's young professionals have nowhere between a roadside dhaba and an expensive coffee franchise. The dhaba lacks comfort and hygiene; the franchise charges PKR 800 for a drink most people don't actually want.
solution: Clean, fast, air-conditioned chai cafes with a fixed 12-item menu, PKR 150–350 price band, and a 90-second serve time. Standardised recipes and central prep keep quality identical across branches.
businessModel: Company-owned cafes. Average ticket PKR 480, 60% gross margin on beverages, 45% on food. A branch breaks even at month 7 on average.
targetMarket: Urban 20–35 year olds in Karachi's commercial districts — an estimated 1.2M people within delivery radius of our current branches.
competition: Quetta cafes on price, international coffee chains on ambience. Nobody owns the middle at scale.
milestones: Third branch opened March 2025, profitable since month 9. Central kitchen commissioned January 2026.
useOfFunds: Two new branches in Clifton and Gulshan (60%), central kitchen expansion (25%), hiring an operations manager (15%).
founderBio: Ex-operations lead at a national restaurant group. Ran the first Chai Theory branch himself for a year before opening the second.

name: SastaBazar
oneLiner: Wholesale grocery marketplace for kiryana stores in Lahore, moving PKR 3.5M in monthly orders.
problem: Lahore's 40,000 kiryana stores buy stock through a chain of middlemen, losing 8–12% margin and half a working day per restock trip.
solution: An Urdu-first ordering app plus next-morning delivery from our own micro-warehouse. Store owners order at 10pm, stock arrives before opening.
businessModel: 6–9% margin on goods sold, plus placement fees from FMCG brands wanting shelf priority. Average order value PKR 18,000.
targetMarket: Kiryana and general stores in Lahore — 40,000 stores, PKR 30B+ annual restocking spend.
competition: Traditional wholesale markets and two funded B2B players focused on Karachi. We win on delivery reliability and Urdu-first UX.
milestones: Crossed 600 active stores in April 2026. Repeat order rate 78%.
useOfFunds: Second micro-warehouse (40%), inventory working capital (40%), two field sales hires (20%).
founderBio: Former category manager at a leading FMCG distributor. Grew up in her family's kiryana store in Ichhra.

name: Raftar Logistics
oneLiner: Same-day intercity parcel delivery between Lahore, Faisalabad and Islamabad for e-commerce sellers.
problem: Online sellers in Punjab wait 3–5 days for courier delivery between major cities, driving return rates above 20% on cash-on-delivery orders.
solution: Fixed daily line-haul vans between Lahore, Faisalabad and Islamabad with last-mile rider fleets in each city. Order by noon, delivered same evening.
businessModel: Per-parcel pricing PKR 220–350 with volume tiers. COD collection fee of 1%. 34% net margin per parcel at current volume.
targetMarket: Punjab's 25,000+ active online sellers shipping intercity daily.
competition: National couriers on coverage; we beat them 4x on speed within our triangle and match on price.
milestones: COD return rate for our sellers dropped from 22% to 9%. Islamabad route added November 2025.
useOfFunds: Two additional line-haul vans (50%), rider fleet expansion (30%), route software (20%).
founderBio: Third-generation transporter. Digitised his family's goods-forwarding business before starting Raftar.

name: Ustaad Academy
oneLiner: Matric and FSc exam prep in Urdu, sold through low-cost monthly subscriptions.
problem: Board exam students outside major cities rely on academies charging PKR 5,000+ monthly, taught inconsistently, with no Urdu-medium digital alternative worth using.
solution: Recorded video courses by top board examiners, weekly live problem-solving sessions, and past-paper drills — all in Urdu, at PKR 750 a month, working on 3G.
businessModel: Monthly subscriptions with a 40% take rate on partner-academy bundles. Blended CAC PKR 380 against LTV of PKR 4,100.
targetMarket: 3.2M matric and FSc students sitting Punjab board exams annually.
competition: English-first edtech apps and physical academies. Neither serves the Urdu-medium board student at this price.
milestones: Students using the platform for 3+ months improved board scores by an average of 11%.
useOfFunds: Content production for Sindh board syllabus (45%), performance marketing (35%), two academic hires (20%).
founderBio: Taught FSc physics for eight years and ran Lahore's highest-rated YouTube physics channel before founding Ustaad.

name: SehatLink
oneLiner: Lab test booking and home sample collection across Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
problem: Getting a blood test in the twin cities means queueing at a lab, opaque pricing, and paper reports that get lost between doctors.
solution: Book any of 400+ tests in the app, a certified phlebotomist collects the sample at home, and digital reports arrive with plain-Urdu explanations of results.
businessModel: 15–22% commission from partner labs plus a PKR 300 home collection fee. Corporate wellness packages for offices launched in 2025.
targetMarket: 2.3M residents of Islamabad and Rawalpindi; 60,000+ diagnostic tests performed daily in the twin cities.
competition: Lab walk-ins and two national aggregator apps with thin coverage here. We own the phlebotomist network locally.
milestones: 12 corporate wellness contracts signed. Partnered with three of the five largest lab networks.
useOfFunds: Phlebotomist fleet expansion to Lahore (50%), app rebuild (25%), corporate sales team (25%).
founderBio: MBBS with five years in hospital operations at a major Islamabad hospital. Built SehatLink after watching patients carry the same lost paper reports repeatedly.

name: Kapraa
oneLiner: D2C menswear basics brand shipping 4,000+ orders a month from Faisalabad's textile belt.
problem: Quality men's basics in Pakistan are either imported at import prices or local with inconsistent sizing and fabric that fades in five washes.
solution: Combed-cotton tees, polos and trousers cut to a consistent Pakistani fit, made in Faisalabad, sold direct at half the price of mall brands.
businessModel: D2C via website and Instagram, 55% gross margin, AOV PKR 3,400. COD is 70% of orders with a 6% return rate — well below category average.
targetMarket: Urban men 22–40 buying online — a segment spending an estimated PKR 25B annually.
competition: Mall brands on brand recognition, Instagram sellers on price. We win on fit consistency and fabric quality at mid price.
milestones: Crossed 100,000 lifetime orders in May 2026. Launched trousers line February 2026.
useOfFunds: Fabric inventory for winter line (50%), performance marketing (30%), a Lahore try-on studio (20%).
founderBio: Grew up on the floor of his father's knitwear export unit. Started Kapraa with rejected-for-export stock and PKR 400,000.

name: FasalTech
oneLiner: Soil testing and crop advisory for mid-size farms in central Punjab, paid per acre per season.
problem: Punjab's farmers over-apply fertiliser by 30–40% because nobody tests their soil, burning cash and yield at the same time.
solution: Field teams run on-site soil tests and deliver a per-acre fertiliser and irrigation plan via WhatsApp voice notes in Punjabi, with mid-season check-ins.
businessModel: PKR 1,200 per acre per season. Input suppliers pay referral margin on precisely-dosed fertiliser orders. 68% of farms renew for the next season.
targetMarket: 180,000 mid-size farms (12–100 acres) in central Punjab.
competition: Government extension services on paper, nobody in practice. Input dealers advise but are conflicted — they profit from overuse.
milestones: Client farms averaged 12% yield improvement and 25% lower fertiliser spend across two wheat seasons.
useOfFunds: Six more field agronomists (55%), a second soil lab in Sahiwal (30%), advisory app (15%).
founderBio: Agricultural sciences graduate from UAF. Ran extension programs for a fertiliser company before switching sides to work for the farmer.

name: Dastarkhwan
oneLiner: Home-style office lunch subscriptions delivering 900 meals a day in Islamabad.
problem: Office workers in Islamabad choose daily between expensive restaurant delivery and tiffin services with no hygiene standards or menu variety.
solution: A central kitchen producing a rotating 20-dish weekly menu, delivered to offices on subscription at PKR 350 a meal, with published hygiene audits.
businessModel: Weekly and monthly meal subscriptions, 38% gross margin. Corporate accounts (10+ meals daily) are 55% of volume and churn under 3% monthly.
targetMarket: 250,000 office workers in Islamabad's commercial sectors.
competition: Informal tiffin services and food delivery apps. We beat one on consistency and the other on price.
milestones: Kitchen capacity doubled January 2026. First 1,000-meal day in June 2026.
useOfFunds: Second kitchen in Rawalpindi (50%), delivery fleet (30%), corporate sales (20%).
founderBio: Former hotel F&B manager. Started Dastarkhwan from her own kitchen with 40 daily meals for one office building.

name: PartsDukan
oneLiner: Online auto parts marketplace with verified fitment for Pakistan's most-driven cars.
problem: Car owners get quoted three different prices for the same part and often receive the wrong one — fitment data for local models simply doesn't exist online.
solution: A catalogue of 18,000 parts mapped to exact make-model-year for the 30 most common cars in Pakistan, with a fitment guarantee and 48-hour delivery.
businessModel: Marketplace take rate of 12% plus fulfilment fees. Own-inventory fast-movers carry 28% margin. AOV PKR 6,200.
targetMarket: 3.8M registered passenger cars in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad.
competition: Physical parts markets and general marketplaces with no fitment data. Our catalogue is the moat.
milestones: Fitment-error return rate under 2%. Workshop bulk-ordering portal launched April 2026.
useOfFunds: Fast-mover inventory (45%), catalogue expansion to bikes (30%), workshop sales team (25%).
founderBio: Ran his family's parts shop in Plaza Market for six years, then spent two years building the fitment database that became PartsDukan.

name: Qaabil
oneLiner: Job-ready IT bootcamps in Lahore with income-share agreements and an 81% placement rate.
problem: Pakistan produces 25,000 CS graduates a year but companies still can't hire — degrees don't teach the stack employers actually use.
solution: 16-week full-time bootcamps in web development and QA, taught by working engineers, paid via income-share after the graduate lands a job above PKR 60k/month.
businessModel: Income-share agreements of 12% of salary for 18 months, capped at PKR 350,000. Upfront-fee track for self-funded students is 30% of enrolment.
targetMarket: Fresh graduates and career-switchers 20–28; roughly 400,000 people enter this pool annually.
competition: Short-course academies with no placement accountability. Our incentive alignment is the difference.
growthPct: New cohort size up 20% each quarter
milestones: Hiring partnerships with 40 software houses. First QA cohort fully placed before graduation.
useOfFunds: ISA financing pool (60%), second campus in Johar Town (25%), placement team (15%).
founderBio: Former engineering manager at a US-remote software house. Hired 60+ engineers and got tired of interviewing unprepared graduates, so he built the pipeline himself.

name: Hisaab
oneLiner: Urdu bookkeeping app for small retailers — 6,000 shops track credit and cash daily.
problem: Small shopkeepers run credit ledgers in paper registers — money gets lost, disputes are constant, and no formal lender will touch a business with no records.
solution: A dead-simple Urdu app for udhaar tracking, daily cash tally and automatic WhatsApp payment reminders to customers. Works offline, syncs when connected.
businessModel: Freemium: core ledger free, PKR 500/month for reminders, reports and multi-user. Transaction data (with consent) powers a lending-referral pipeline with two partner fintechs.
targetMarket: 2M+ small retailers nationwide; 300,000 in Karachi alone.
competition: Paper registers and two regional ledger apps. Retention is the battleground — ours is 64% at month 6.
milestones: PKR 900M in receivables tracked through the app. Lending referral pilot live with 120 shops.
useOfFunds: Field onboarding teams (45%), Android app performance work (30%), lending pipeline integrations (25%).
founderBio: Ex-product manager at a Pakistani fintech unicorn. Built Hisaab's first version in a weekend for his uncle's general store.

name: Thanda Meetha
oneLiner: Packaged traditional desserts sold through 300+ retail stores in Punjab.
problem: Traditional desserts like kheer and gajar ka halwa are either homemade or sold loose at sweet shops with no shelf life, no branding and no consistency.
solution: Factory-packed single-serve traditional desserts with 21-day refrigerated shelf life, stocked in supermarket chillers next to imported yogurts at half the price.
businessModel: Distribution through modern trade and top general stores. 42% gross margin ex-factory. Listed in two national supermarket chains.
targetMarket: Urban grocery shoppers across Punjab; the packaged dessert category is growing 18% annually.
competition: Loose sweet shops and imported desserts. We're the only branded local player in the chiller.
milestones: Second national chain listing signed May 2026. Ramzan season sold out three weeks early.
useOfFunds: Cold-chain van fleet (40%), production line automation (40%), trade marketing (20%).
founderBio: Food technologist who spent six years in dairy manufacturing before productising her grandmother's kheer recipe.

name: Gharana
oneLiner: Verified home services — plumbers, electricians, AC techs — completing 2,000 jobs a month in Karachi.
problem: Finding a plumber in Karachi means calling around, no-shows, made-up prices and letting an unverified stranger into your home.
solution: Background-checked technicians, fixed published prices for 120 common jobs, booked in the app with a 2-hour arrival window and a 30-day workmanship guarantee.
businessModel: 20% commission per job plus PKR 5,000/month technician subscription for lead priority. Average job value PKR 2,800.
targetMarket: 1.5M middle and upper-middle income households in Karachi.
competition: Word-of-mouth technicians and one funded competitor focused on beauty services. Home repair is unclaimed.
milestones: 480 verified technicians onboarded. AC servicing season did 3x normal volume.
useOfFunds: Technician recruitment and verification (40%), Lahore launch (40%), customer app v2 (20%).
founderBio: Former operations lead at a ride-hailing company's Karachi office. Applied the same supply-side playbook to home services.

name: Mitti
oneLiner: D2C skincare made from indigenous ingredients, 2,500 orders a month and growing.
problem: Pakistani skincare buyers choose between expensive imports and local products with undisclosed ingredients and no dermatological testing.
solution: A tight 9-SKU line built on multani mitti, rosewater and cold-pressed oils — dermatologically tested, fully disclosed ingredients, priced PKR 900–2,200.
businessModel: D2C website and Instagram, 62% gross margin, AOV PKR 2,900. Subscribe-and-save is 18% of revenue and climbing.
targetMarket: Urban women 20–40 buying skincare online — a PKR 15B and fast-growing segment.
competition: Imported brands on prestige, bazaar products on price. We own 'trusted local' with published lab tests.
milestones: Sold out launch batch in 11 days. Featured by three of Pakistan's top beauty creators unpaid.
useOfFunds: Inventory depth (45%), content and creator marketing (35%), pharmacy retail pilot (20%).
founderBio: Pharmacist by training. Formulated Mitti's first three products herself and had them independently lab-tested before selling a single unit.

name: MurghiKhana
oneLiner: Farm-to-door antibiotic-free chicken, delivering to 1,800 households in Lahore weekly.
problem: Urban families increasingly distrust commercial broiler chicken but have no reliable, affordable alternative to the neighbourhood murghi wala.
solution: Contracted small farms raise antibiotic-free birds to our protocol; we process, chill and deliver cut-to-order within 24 hours of slaughter on weekly subscriptions.
businessModel: Weekly subscription boxes PKR 1,800–4,500. 30% gross margin after farm cost and processing. Subscriber churn 4% monthly.
targetMarket: Upper-middle income households in Lahore — 400,000 households, protein spend PKR 15,000+/month.
competition: Wet market butchers on price and habit. We win on trust, and our farm audits are public.
milestones: Contracted farm network grew to 14 farms. Launched marinated ready-to-cook line March 2026.
useOfFunds: Processing facility upgrade (50%), cold-chain delivery vans (30%), farm network expansion (20%).
founderBio: Veterinary sciences graduate who managed poultry operations for a feed conglomerate before building the supply chain he wished existed.

name: Safar Stays
oneLiner: Managed guesthouse network in northern Pakistan with 68% average occupancy.
problem: Domestic tourism to the north has exploded but booking a room in Hunza or Skardu still means WhatsApp roulette with unverified properties and no refunds.
solution: We sign underperforming guesthouses, standardise them to a published checklist, professionally photograph them, and run pricing, booking and payments centrally.
businessModel: 18–25% of room revenue on managed properties. Instant-confirmation bookings with digital payment, prepaid, with a clear refund policy.
targetMarket: 1.5M+ domestic tourists visiting Gilgit-Baltistan annually, growing 20%+ a year.
competition: Direct WhatsApp booking and international OTAs with stale inventory. Our managed model controls quality end to end.
milestones: 68% average occupancy across the network vs 40% regional average. Skardu cluster added 2025.
useOfFunds: Property onboarding in Swat and Naran (50%), booking platform v2 (30%), regional ops hires (20%).
founderBio: Former hotel revenue manager from Gilgit. Managed his family's guesthouse to 90% seasonal occupancy before productising the playbook.
